newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Queensland cuts payroll, land tax in 97/98 budget.
newsitem.headline: Queensland cuts payroll, land tax in 97/98 budget.

text.p: The state of Queensland introduced land tax concessions and increased the threshold for payroll tax in its 1997/98 (July/June) budget released Tuesday.
The payroll tax threshold will be increased by A$50,000 to A$850,000 from January 1, 1998, at a cost to revenue of A$3.2 million in 1997/98 and A$6.5 million in a full year, the budget papers show.
Treasurer Joan Sheldon told state parliament the land tax concession, involving three components, was broadly equivalent to a 10 percent reduction in land tax across the board.

Under the package, the tax exemption threshold for companies, trusts and absentees will increased by A$40,000 to A$100,000, the statuatory deductions for individuals will increase to A$200,000 from A$160,000 and a general rebate of five percent will apply to all land tax payers in 1997/98.

The government said the cost to revenue in 1997/98 was estimated at A$20 million. "The land tax and payroll tax concessions are key components of the coaltion's employment, training and small business strategy, designed to minimise business costs and stimulate real jobs growth," Sheldon said.
